# SystemAllocator

An allocator that asks the operating system for pages.

```rux
pub struct SystemAllocator {
    // private fields
}
```

Carries no state: every instance behaves identically, and one may be created wherever it is needed rather than
passed around. It is `Copy` for that reason.
Page-granular, so a small allocation costs a whole page. Use it as the backing store for an arena or a pool
rather than for many small values directly.

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>SystemAllocator</code></h3>

```rux
pub func SystemAllocator() -> SystemAllocator
```

Constructs a stateless system allocator.
The result is structural and copyable. Borrow it as `&var Allocator` when a temporary interface view is
sufficient; no adapter or owning conversion is required.

**Returns**: the allocator, which holds no state of its own

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/System.rux#L56)

## Implements Allocator

`SystemAllocator` conforms to [`Allocator`](/docs/api/allocator/allocator).

<h3 id="allocate"><code>Allocate</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Allocate(
    self: &SystemAllocator,
    layout: Layout
) -> (*var opaque) ! AllocError
```

Takes storage matching `layout` from the operating system.
`result` receives the address when this reports `None`. A zero-sized layout gives the shared empty block and
takes nothing from the system.
Reports `Unsupported` for an alignment larger than the total the request would occupy, `OutOfMemory` when the
system refuses.
The storage is the caller's until [`Deallocate`](/docs/api/allocator/system-allocator#deallocate) takes it back with an equal layout.

| Name     | Type     | Description                   |
| -------- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `layout` | `Layout` | the size and alignment wanted |

**Returns**: the address of the storage, or why none was taken

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/System.rux#L72)

<h3 id="deallocate"><code>Deallocate</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Deallocate(
    self: &SystemAllocator,
    block: *var opaque,
    layout: Layout
) -> ! AllocError
```

Gives the storage behind `block` back to the operating system.
`layout` must equal the one the block was allocated with. Reports `InvalidBlock` when the header is not
there or does not agree with the layout, which catches a foreign pointer and a mismatched size before either
reaches the page layer.
Every pointer into the block becomes invalid.

| Name     | Type          | Description                        |
| -------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `block`  | `*var opaque` | an address this allocator returned |
| `layout` | `Layout`      | the layout it was allocated with   |

**Returns**: nothing when the release was accepted, or why it was refused

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/System.rux#L113)

<h3 id="reallocate"><code>Reallocate</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Reallocate(
    self: &SystemAllocator,
    block: *var opaque,
    oldLayout: Layout,
    newLayout: Layout
) -> (*var opaque) ! AllocError
```

Changes the size of a block by taking a new one and copying what fits.
The two layouts must share an alignment; anything else reports `Unsupported` rather than moving the block to
a different one. On success the original block is released and `result` holds the new address, which is
generally not the old one.
This allocator never grows a block in place, even when the page it sits in has room: doing so would need a
free-list it deliberately does not keep.
The old pointer is invalid once this succeeds. On failure it is untouched and still the caller's.

| Name        | Type          | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `block`     | `*var opaque` | the existing allocation's address                     |
| `oldLayout` | `Layout`      | the layout `block` was allocated with                 |
| `newLayout` | `Layout`      | the layout wanted, which must have the same alignment |

**Returns**: the address the block is at afterwards, or why it was not resized

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/System.rux#L136)

## Related

<h3 id="system-block-header"><code>SystemBlockHeader</code></h3>

```rux
pub struct SystemBlockHeader {
    // private fields
}
```

What a system allocation records about itself, immediately before the address the caller sees.
Never constructed by a caller. The magic is checked on release, which is what turns a mismatched or foreign
pointer into a reported `InvalidBlock` rather than a corrupted heap.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/System.rux#L22)

<h3 id="system-block-magic"><code>SystemBlockMagic</code></h3>

```rux
pub const SystemBlockMagic: uint64 = 0x52757841_6C6C6F63;
```

The pattern a valid system block header carries.
Chosen to be unlikely in ordinary data, so a pointer that was never one of these is very unlikely to look like
one. This is a check against a mistake, not against an adversary.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/System.rux#L37)
